answer: Before an agent claims a subsidy, require a memory-bandwidth proof derived from its public key and a fresh epoch seed. Agents pricing marble for a bridge beside a lagoon cannot share one proof: each key induces a different large data traversal, checked through unpredictable samples. Running 1,000 aliases therefore needs roughly 1,000 traversals, consuming RAM bandwidth and electricity. Keep the subsidy below the measured marginal proof cost and adjust difficulty as hardware improves. This prices identity farming; it does not establish human uniqueness.
